question: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
explanation: The danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus always considered dangerous?
choice_a: Because it is out of the driver's field of vision entirely
choice_c: Because students always exit on that side
choice_d: Because the driver cannot open the door on that side
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: The outside left and right side flat mirrors on a school bus should be adjusted so the driver can see how far behind the bus?
explanation: Flat mirrors should be adjusted to show 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along with the sides of the bus and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: What is the primary purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: To check tire tread depth during a pre-trip inspection
choice_b: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_c: To see traffic approaching from behind in the adjacent lane
choice_d: To see the front bumper danger zone and the side danger zones not visible by direct vision
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus and the danger zone areas to the left and right side, none of which are visible by direct vision.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1 to 10-2

question: The blind spot directly behind a school bus's rear bumper, monitored using the overhead inside rearview mirror and exterior mirrors, could extend up to how far?
explanation: There is a large blind spot beginning at the rear bumper that could extend up to 400 feet or more behind the bus, which drivers must monitor using the exterior side mirrors.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: According to the manual, when should you activate alternating flashing amber warning lights when approaching a school bus stop?
choice_a: Only after the bus has come to a complete stop
choice_b: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the stop, or in accordance with state law
choice_c: At least 500 feet before the stop
choice_d: Amber lights are only used at night
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: When stopping to load or unload students along a route, how far away from the students should the front bumper of the school bus be positioned?
explanation: The bus should come to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop, forcing students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: After unloading students along a route, how far should students walk from the side of the bus before the driver pulls away?
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to have students exit and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students before pulling away.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: What should students do if they cannot immediately locate a dropped object near the school bus during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Ask another student to retrieve it
choice_b: Retrieve the object immediately before boarding
choice_c: Wait next to the object until the driver notices
choice_d: Leave the object, move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, and try to get the driver's attention
explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, then attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve the object, since stopping to pick it up can cause the student to disappear from the driver's sight at a dangerous moment.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-5

question: When students must cross the roadway after exiting a school bus, how far in front of the right corner of the bumper should they walk before stopping to look for the driver's signal?
explanation: Students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the bus, and wait for the driver's signal before crossing.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: As a general rule, how far off the road should a designated safe place be located during a school bus evacuation, in the direction of oncoming traffic?
explanation: A safe place should be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials during a school bus evacuation, how far upwind should students be led?
explanation: Students should be led upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: Under which of these conditions does the manual say the driver MUST evacuate the school bus?
choice_a: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_b: Whenever the bus is more than 10 minutes behind schedule
explanation: Mandatory evacuation conditions include the bus being on fire or threatened by fire, stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, imminent danger of collision, the bus's position changing to increase danger, or a need to evacuate due to a hazardous materials spill.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: According to the manual, what is generally the best way to maintain student safety and control during an emergency or impending crisis situation?
choice_a: Always evacuate the bus immediately regardless of circumstances
choice_b: Call 911 and wait without giving students any instructions
choice_c: Allow students to decide individually whether to exit
choice_d: Keep students on the bus if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury
explanation: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency or impending crisis, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: What type of railroad-highway crossing has no traffic control device, requiring the driver to recognize the crossing, search for a train, and decide whether it is safe to cross?
explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control device; the decision to proceed rests entirely on the driver recognizing the crossing, searching for a train, and deciding if there is sufficient clear space to cross safely.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: When stopping a school bus at a railroad-highway crossing, how close to the nearest rail should the bus stop?
choice_a: No closer than 25 feet and no farther than 75 feet
choice_b: No closer than 5 feet and no farther than 20 feet
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_d: Exactly 10 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The bus should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, at the point offering the best view of the tracks.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: If the crossing gate comes down after a school bus has already started crossing the tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Honk the horn and wait for the gate to rise
choice_c: Stop immediately on the tracks and wait
choice_d: Drive through the gate even if it means breaking it
explanation: If the gate comes down after the bus has started across, the driver should drive through it even if it means breaking the gate, rather than stopping on the tracks.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: As a general rule of thumb for containment or storage area at a railroad crossing, how many extra feet should be added to the length of the school bus?
explanation: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area needed to clear the tracks on the other side.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: If a student causes a serious behavior problem while the bus is moving, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Continue driving and ignore the behavior
choice_b: Radio the police immediately without stopping
choice_c: Stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road
choice_d: Pull over only at the next scheduled stop
explanation: To handle serious problems, the driver should stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road, such as a parking lot or driveway, before addressing the situation.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: Under Department of Transportation requirements referenced in the manual, air brake vehicles including buses must have antilock braking systems if built on or after what date?
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems on air brake vehicles, including trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies, built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: In emergency braking on a school bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_c: Applying steady, firm pressure to the brake pedal
choice_d: Braking the same way as always
explanation: Drivers should brake the same way regardless of whether the bus has ABS, but in emergency braking, they should not pump the brakes on a bus equipped with ABS.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9 to 10-10

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have, which drivers must monitor with mirrors during turns?
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so drivers need to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor it.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: What does the manual say about backing a school bus?
choice_a: It is only allowed at school parking lots
choice_b: It is strongly discouraged and should only be done when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle
choice_c: It requires no lookout if mirrors are properly adjusted
choice_d: It is preferred over pulling forward whenever possible
explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged; the driver should back only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle, and never when students are outside the bus.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10
